title: Java SPI
context: What is the Java Service Provider Interface (SPI), and how do frameworks use it?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: SPI lets a library define an interface and load its implementations found on the classpath. The implementing jar lists its class names in `META-INF/services/<interface name>`. `ServiceLoader` reads those files and creates the instances. This decouples the core from its plugins: JDBC drivers are found this way. The trade-off is that providers are found and created lazily at run time, so a broken provider fails only when it is loaded. Tests should load every provider.

points.title: Discovery by file
points.why: Implementations are listed in META-INF/services, and ServiceLoader finds them without code changes.

points.title: Run-time failures
points.why: A broken provider only fails when loaded, so load each one in a test.
